title: transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt placement in a child complicated by perforated roux-en-y portoenterostomy
display_name: Transjugular Intrahepatic Portosystemic Shunt Placement in a Child Complicated by Perforated Roux-en-Y Portoenterostomy
abstract: portal hypertension is one of the major complications of hepatic failure. since the transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt (tips) was pioneered for clinical use in 1982 by colapinto et al. (1), it has been increasingly employed in advanced liver disease to relieve recurrent variceal bleeding or intractable ascites. tips has proved to be effective in reducing the portosystemic pressure gradient and thus in reducing incidence of variceal bleeding (2,3). however, complication rates can be high, depending on the technique used and degree of experience in the use of the tips at different institutions. a recent comprehensive review found that the tips carries a total complication rate ranging from 4% to 77% in adults (4). the tips has been predominantly used in adults, and review of the literature reveals few reports of successful placement in children. we report placement of a tips in a very young child with a unique life-threatening complication. case report case 1 the patient is a 21-month-old girl who was diagnosed with biliary atresia and malrotation soon after birth. at seven weeks of age, she underwent the kasai portoenterostomy along with the ladd's procedure in the philippines. subsequently, she had several episodes of ascending cholangitis and no significant improvement in bile flow. she moved to hawaii at 20 months of age for medical treatment, where she continued to have significant ascites and three documented episodes of gastrointestinal bleeding. her hemoglobin dropped to 5 g/dl, requiring multiple transfusions; her international normalized ratio was 1.6; and her ammonia levels reached a high of 131 mol/l, although she was without clinical signs of encephalopathy. her upper gastrointestinal bleeding was refractory to medications and repeated endoscopic sclerotherapy. she was subsequently transferred to our institution 1 month later for further management of her esophageal variceal bleeds and end-stage liver disease. physical examination on admission revealed a thin, somnolent 21-month-old girl in no acute distress. her temperature was 37.7 c, heart rate 131 bpm, blood pressure 92/57 mmhg, and respiratory rate 52/min. her height was 81 cm (50th percentile), abdominal girth 60 cm, and weight 11.9 kg (25th-50th percentile). she had icteric sclera and jaundice. her heartbeat was tachycardic with a regular rhythm, and she had a grade ii-vi crescendo-decrescendo murmur, which was loudest in the left lower sternal border. her lungs were clear to auscultation bilaterally. her abdomen was markedly distended with ascites with a palpable liver 7 cm below the right costal margin in the midclavicular line, extending to 3 cm below the left costal margin in the midclavicular line. the spleen tip was not palpable. examination of the extremities revealed clubbing without cyanosis or edema. results of a neurologic examination were appropriate for the patient's age, without asterixis. significant laboratory findings on admission include: white blood cell count 22,000/ l, hematocrit 32.2%, platelets 314,000/ l, total bilirubin 6.6 mg/dl, aspartate aminotransferase 144 iu/l, alanine aminotrasferase 112 iu/l, alkaline phosphatase 610 iu/l, -glutamyltransferase 392 iu/l, total protein 5.7 g/dl, albumin 2.2 g/dl, prothrombin time 13.9 seconds, partial thromboplastin time 24.1 seconds, total cholesterol 164 mg/dl, and triglycerides 78 mg/dl. on arrival, the patient was listed with the united network for organ sharing after approval as a liver transplant candidate. while awaiting an available donor organ, she continued to bleed with guaiac-positive burgundy stools. abdominal ultrasound revealed massive intrahepatic biliary ductal dilatation, inferior vena cava with good flow, and patent portal vein with hepatopetal flow. size of portal veins was not mentioned. endoscopy showed multiple, enlarged varices sized 3 to 4+, and a decision was made to place a tips as a bridge to the transplant to avoid recurrent gastrointestinal bleeding. on the fourth hospital day, a 10-mm 68-mm schneider wallstent schneider, minneapolis, mn, u.s.a. was placed by interventional radiology. under fluoroscopic guidance, the right internal jugular vein was accessed, the right hepatic vein was catheterized, and the wedged hepatic co2 venogram performed. difficulty was encountered accessing the portal vein because of extensive fibrosis in the region of the portahepatis, presumably related to the kasai procedure. several attempts were made using the rosch-uchida and the colapinto needle systems to push through the woody liver parenchyma before the right portal vein was accessed. the preprocedure portal vein pressure, which correlates with the hepatic wedge pressure, was 32 mmhg. a venogram performed before placement of the stent showed the portal venous anatomy (fig. 1). the stent was then expanded to 8 mm across the parenchymal tract, bridging the right hepatic vein to the right portal vein (figs. 2,3). a final portal venogram was performed, and atrial (6 mmhg) and portal (10 mmhg) pressures were obtained by placing a straight flush catheter within the splenic vein. the patient tolerated the procedure fairly well except for a 5-minute hypotensive episode during the procedure, which was presumably caused by variceal bleeding. this resolved with volume support and tips deployment. no other immediate complications were noted. results of a portogram performed before deployment of the stent showed extravasation of contrast, presumably from coronary vein varices. results of a portogram performed after the tips was deployed showed decompression of the coronary vein varix with adequate flow through the tips. within 36 hours after the tips was placed, the patient developed a fever of 39.2 c, increasing abdominal girth, a white count of 26,400/ l, and a decrease in hematocrit from 26.2% to 22.1%. there were no further episodes of variceal bleeding, documented by nasogastric aspirates, but there was another source of bleeding evidenced by the patient's decreasing hematocrit. findings in doppler ultrasonography showed a large quantity of ascites and a patent tips shunt with good cephalad flow (figs. 4,5). results of abdominal x-rays taken in the upright and lateral-decubitus positions showed no free air but evidence of a distended small and large bowel consistent with an ileus. the patient had been receiving ceftriaxone for staphylococcus aureus infection in the line since before placement of the tips. her antibiotic coverage was changed at this time to ampicillin, gentamicin, and clindamycin. blood cultures from the 2 days after placement of the tips became positive for candida tropicalis, and she was given amphotericin b and flucytosine. on the patient's eighth hospital day, she was stable on antifungal drugs and successfully underwent an orthotopic liver transplant. the source of her fungemia was the end of the stent protruding through the anterior wall of the right portal vein into the lumen of her roux-en-y portoenterostomy. the stent was clotted and purulent material was found at the end, along with a moderate amount of bloody ascites. the patient's suprahepatic inferior vena cava was exposed without difficulty, but a congenital absence of the intrahepatic inferior vena cava was noticed. the larger-than-average common hepatic artery was aberrant in origin, arising directly from the aorta, superior to the usual position of the celiac trunk. additional intraoperative findings include a preduodenal portal vein, bowel malrotation, and polysplenia. the patient received a liver from a 7-year-old donor, which was placed in the piggyback position. her roux-en-y was revised, and a biliary catheter was placed, from which golden brown bile flowed immediately after anastomosis. she began treatment with methylprednisolone, fk-506, dextran, heparin, and aspirin. her liver enzymes peaked on postoperative day 2, then dropped progressively. she remained afebrile and received amphotericin b for 10 days. on postoperative day 3, her blood cultures were positive for enterobacter, which was treated with ciprofloxacin and gentamicin. on postoperative day 7, her white cell count returned to normal and liver function test values continued to improve. she remained afebrile and was tolerating a clear liquid diet. fifteen days after transplant, she returned to the operating room for lysis of adhesions that had caused a small bowel obstruction. twenty-four days after transplant, she was tolerating a regular diet and was having regular bowel movements. she was discharged home in stable condition. the patient continues to do well with good graft function 6 months after her liver transplantation. discussion we have presented a unique case of the use of a tips in a young child, complicated by erosion of the stent through her portal vein into her roux-en-y portoenterostomy. there has been little experience with the tips in children, and there is no prior description of stent erosion through vessels or perforation of the roux-en-y by the tips. most common complications with tips described in adults are stenosis and thrombosis, encephalopathy, and recurrent variceal bleeding. of the 4% to 77% total complication rate described by freedman et al., immediate complications were less than 10%, whereas late shunt occlusion occurred in 15% to 77%. procedural mortality was found to be 0% to 2%, with death usually caused by intraoperative myocardial infarction or intraperitoneal hemorrhage. the thirty-day mortality rate ranged between 7% and 45%, with death usually caused by complications related to the patient's end-stage liver disease. shunt occlusion was often the main cause of rebleeding, requiring dilatation of the shunt or placement of additional shunts (4). a popular theory for the etiology of occlusion is pseudointimal hyperplasia in the shunt (5,6). hepatic encephalopathy is a potential complication, resulting from diversion of a significant amount of blood from hepatic metabolism. incidence for hepatic encephalopathy varies from 5% to 35%. fortunately, most respond well to medical therapy, only occasionally requiring treatment of an occluded shunt (4). less common complications are thrombosis in the portal or jugular vein (0-9%) and acute thrombosis in the stent (0-10%). shortening or incomplete placement of the shunt is reported in up to 10% of cases, and stent misplacement or migration occurs in 0% to 8%. there have been documented migrations of stents into the suprahepatic inferior vena cava, too far into the main portal vein, into the pulmonary artery, and into the right atrium (7,8). poor positioning of the stent may cause problems with cross-clamping during liver transplantation, because clamping is done at the portion of the suprahepatic inferior vena cava below the diaphragm and across the portal vein (7). transcapsular needle puncture occurs 5% to 30% of the time, mostly without any serious consequences. the puncturing of the liver capsule, the hepatic artery (0-1.5%), and kidney (0-1.5%) can cause hemoperitoneum. a potentially fatal complication is massive intraperitoneal hemorrhage from rupture of the portal vein, resulting from extrahepatic puncture and balloon dilation of the portal vein (0-1.3%). occasionally the biliary system is punctured (0-10%) causing hemobilia. additional reported complications in the use of a tips include acute renal failure caused by contrast (0-4%), infection-sepsis (0-10%), coagulopathy (0-4%), hemolysis (0-1.5%), progressive liver failure, and acute hepatic decompensation (4). several factors predisposed the patient in this case to the potentially fatal complication, including her small size, history of kasai procedure, and abnormalities in the perihepatic vessels. the stress placed on her small hypoplastic portal vessels by dilatation with a 10-mm stent was probably the major contributing factor to perforation of the vein. is there an age below which the anatomy of the patient is too small for placement of a tips? the small diameter of vessels in children is an obstacle for insertion of the stent and increases the risk of shunt stenosis and thromboses. the size of stent used in the above case was that commonly used in adult patients. the wallstent used may have been too wide and too long for this patient's portal vein, making it susceptible to erosion through her vein into the adjacent roux-en-y portoenterostomy. in addition, there has not been enough experience to know whether children as young as she have a more delicate venous anatomy. berger et al. (9) used a miniaturized puncture set, with the maximum diameter of the introducer sheath at 7.5 french, for introducing the smallest palmaz stents. theoretically, shorter stents appropriate for the smaller child would work the same; however, there may be a minimum width for the stent to avoid unacceptably high rates of stenosis and thrombosis. the few pediatric cases involving placement of a tips in the literature are mostly in older children. five cases were in children ages 10 to 13 (9,10). two younger patients in the literature who successfully underwent placement of a tips were an 18-kg 4-year-old boy and a 13-kg 2.5-year-old boy. they both had bleeding stomal varices from cirrhosis secondary to cholestatic liver disease from hyperalimentation. the 4-year-old had an 8-mm 40-mm wallstent overlapping with an 8-mm 20-mm wallstent for additional length. he had no complications related to the tips for the 1 month he awaited liver transplantation. the 2.5-year-old had an 8-mm 40-mm wallstent, also with no complications for the 10 months of follow-up (11). we recently reported successful insertion of a tips using a smaller (5 mm 40 mm) wallstent in a 9-kg 10-month-old infant, who died 36 hours later because of sepsis that was present before the placement procedure was performed (12). these cases provide encouragement that placing a tips is technically possible in small children, using the smallest of available stents. many children who may need a tips will have biliary atresia, which can greatly complicate the placement procedure. the major cause of hepatic failure in children is biliary atresia, which is a disease associated with progressive liver failure and worsening portal hypertension. findings in a prospective sonographic study indicate that the caliber of portal vein may progressively decrease in patients with biliary atresia and poor hepatobiliary function (13). roux-en-y portoenterostomy is the preferred method of treatment for children with biliary atresia, as in the patient in the case reported. this procedure brings a loop of the small intestines flush against the liver-a procedure that, theoretically, would increase the likelihood of bowel perforation if the liver capsule is punctured by the needle or by the stent. the extensive fibrosis of the surrounding liver caused by the procedure can also make cannulation of the portal vein during placement of a tips extremely difficult. this introduces the question of whether a history of portoenterostomy should be a contraindication for use of a tips. very important is a special awareness that a child with biliary atresia may have ivemark's syndrome (polysplenia). results of studies show that more than 10% of children with biliary atresia have polysplenia, along with the associated abnormalities in perihepatic vessels. our patient had all of these perihepatic abnormalities, including azygous continuation of the inferior vena cava and preduodenal portal vein and anomalous origin of the hepatic artery. they also usually have bowel malrotation, bilaterally bilobed lungs, and congenital heart disease (14,15). most relevant to the placement of a tips is the hypoplastic preduodenal portal vein, which can lead to a greater chance of missed cannulation or perforation. these perihepatic vascular abnormalities have caused complications in liver transplantations in the past (16,17). when a child with end-stage liver disease must receive an intervening procedure (e.g., tips) as a bridge to transplant, what can be done to decrease the likelihood of complications? we offer the following recommendations: fully assess the anatomy of the child, especially possible perihepatic vascular anomalies; optimize the fit between size of the child's venous anatomy and the size of stent used; consider the use of additional imaging studies, which may be helpful in the prevention or rapid diagnosis of stent malposition. real-time sonography in addition to fluoroscopy may be helpful during placement of a tips, and sonography in the early postprocedural period can aid in early diagnosis of complications. in addition, should a complication similar to that in the reported case occur, warning signs may resemble those described in the case report: namely, high white cell count, fever, fungemia, and a drop in hematocrit. other potential signs that were not evident in our patient are peritonitis, free air in the abdomen detected by abdominal x-ray, bacteremia, and abnormal findings in abdominal ultrasonography. with growing experience and awareness of potential complications, we hope to better understand the indications and limitations for use of the tips and to improve on the efficacy and safety of the tips for the management of portal hypertension in young children.fig. 1.: wedged right hepatic co2 venogram demonstrates portal venous anatomy before placement of a transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt.fig. 2.: angioplasty of parenchymal tract between the hepatic and portal veins during creation of a transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt shows extrinsic waist-like impression on the balloon during dilation of fibrotic tissue.fig. 3.: appearance of the 10-mm diameter 68-mm long wall-stent between the right hepatic vein and the portal vein. the stent extends well into the extrahepatic portal vein.fig. 4.: longitudinal ultrasonographic image after a procedure to insert a transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt shows the echogenic stent (arrowheads) extending below liver margins (arrows) into the extrahepatic portal vein.fig. 5.: duplex ultrasonography obtained 1 day after placement of a transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt demonstrates significant unidirectional blood flow within the shunt in its midsegment.

abstract: surgical site infections (ssis), i.e., surgery-related infections that occur within 30 days after surgery without an implant and within one year if an implant is placed, complicate surgical procedures in up to 10% of cases, but an underestimation of the data is possible since about 50% of ssis occur after the hospital discharge. gastrointestinal surgical procedures are among the surgical procedures with the highest risk of ssis, especially when colon surgery is considered. data that were collected from children seem to indicate that the risk of ssis can be higher than in adults. this consensus document describes the use of preoperative antibiotic prophylaxis in neonates and children that are undergoing abdominal surgery and has the purpose of providing guidance to healthcare professionals who take care of children to avoid unnecessary and dangerous use of antibiotics in these patients. the following surgical procedures were analyzed: (1) gastrointestinal endoscopy; (2) abdominal surgery with a laparoscopic or laparotomy approach; (3) small bowel surgery; (4) appendectomy; (5) abdominal wall defect correction interventions; (6) ileo-colic perforation; (7) colorectal procedures; (8) biliary tract procedures; and (9) surgery on the liver or pancreas. thanks to the multidisciplinary contribution of experts belonging to the most important italian scientific societies that take care of neonates and children, this document presents an invaluable reference tool for perioperative antibiotic prophylaxis in the paediatric and neonatal populations.

title: case report: a rare case of benign recurrent intrahepatic cholestasis-type 1 with a novel heterozygous pathogenic variant of atp8b1
display_name: Case Report: A Rare Case of Benign Recurrent Intrahepatic Cholestasis-Type 1 With a Novel Heterozygous Pathogenic Variant of ATP8B1
abstract: benign recurrent intrahepatic cholestasis type 1 (bric1) is a rare autosomal recessive disorder that is characterized by intermittent episodes of jaundice and intense pruritus and caused by pathogenic variants of adenosine triphosphatase phospholipid transporting 8b1 ( atp8b1 ). the presence of genetic heterogeneity in the variants of atp8b1 is suggested. herein, we describe a unique clinical course in a patient with bric1 and a novel heterozygous pathogenic variant of atp8b1 . a 20-year-old japanese man experienced his first cholestasis attack secondary to elevated transaminase at 17 years of age. laboratory examinations showed no evidence of liver injury caused by viral, autoimmune, or inborn or acquired metabolic etiologies. since the patient also had elevated transaminase and hypoalbuminemia, he was treated with ursodeoxycholic acid and prednisolone. however, these treatments did not relieve his symptoms. histopathological assessment revealed marked cholestasis in the hepatocytes, kupffer cells, and bile canaliculi, as well as a well-preserved intralobular bile duct arrangement and strongly expressed bile salt export pump at the canalicular membrane. targeted next-generation sequencing detected a novel heterozygous pathogenic variant of atp8b1 (c.1429 + 2t > g). taken together, the patient was highly suspected of having bric1. ultimately, treatment with 450 mg/day of rifampicin rapidly relieved his symptoms and shortened the symptomatic period.

title: interactions between chronic liver disease and inflammatory bowel disease
display_name: Interactions between chronic liver disease and inflammatory bowel disease
abstract: aliver disease was first recognized in association with idiopathic inflammatory bowel disease (ibd) over a century ago (1).the introduction of better diagnostic tools such as colonoscopy and endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography during the last 25 years has strengthened the association between ibd and chronic hepatobiliary dysfunction, especially primary sclerosing cholangitis (psc).ibd [ulcerative colitis (uc) and crohn's disease (cd)] and psc are both chronic conditions that can result in substantial morbidity and mortality and require coordinated medical and surgical interventions (2-7).since the conditions frequently coexist and the presence of one can alter the natural history or the management of the other, the study of the interaction between these illnesses is of great importance.we review the epidemiology, clinical features, treatment, and prognosis of hepatobiliary diseases associated with ibd as well as the unique clinical features of ibd associated with psc. hepatobiliary dysfunction in ibd prevalencehepatobiliary disease, once thought to be a rare extrainiestinal manifestation of uc and cd, has become increasingly recognized in recent decades ( 3 -9 j.measurement of the true prevalence of liver dysfunction in ibd remains unclear because of imprecise del'initions, differences in diagnostic aggressiveness, and difference? in ibd cohorts studied.for example, if "hepatobiliary disease" is defined as a single abnormal hepatic biochemical parameter, even if transiently elevated.the

title: poor performance of the rapid test for human brucellosis in health facilities in kenya
display_name: Poor performance of the rapid test for human brucellosis in health facilities in Kenya

authorships.name: William A. de Glanville
institutions: Centre for Immunity, Infection and Evolution

authorships.name: Elizabeth A. J. Cook
institutions: Centre for Immunity, Infection and Evolution

authorships.name: Lian F. Thomas
institutions: Centre for Immunity, Infection and Evolution

abstract: human brucellosis is considered to be an important but typically under-diagnosed cause of febrile illness in many low and middle-income countries. in kenya, and throughout east africa, laboratory diagnosis for the disease is based primarily on the febrile antigen brucella agglutination test (fbat), yet few studies of the diagnostic accuracy of this test exist. assessment of the performance of the fbat is essential for its appropriate clinical use, as well as for evaluating surveillance data reported by public health systems. to assess fbat performance, we collected sera from people with symptoms compatible with brucellosis attending two health facilities in busia county, kenya. sera were tested using the fbat and results compared with those from the rose bengal test (rbt), an assay with well-known performance characteristics. positives on either test were confirmed using the classical serum agglutination test (sat)-coombs test combination and a rapid igm/igg lateral flow immunochromatography assay (lfa). a questionnaire focussing on known risk factors for exposure to brucella spp. was also conducted, and relationships with fbat positivity examined using logistic regression. out of 825 recruited individuals, 162 (19.6%) were classified as positive using the fbat. in contrast, only eight (1.0%) were positive using the rbt. of the 162 fbat positives, one (0.62%) had an atypical agglutination in sat and three (1.9%) showed low coombs titres. out of 148 fbat positive individuals tested using the lfa, five (3.4%) were igm positive and none were igg positive. poor or no correlation was observed between fbat results and most established risk factors for brucella infection. we observed substantial disagreement between the fbat and a number of well-known serological tests, with the majority of reactive fbat results appearing to be false positives. poor fbat specificity, combined with a lack of confirmatory testing, strongly suggests overdiagnosis of brucellosis is common in this low prevalence setting. this is expected to have important economic impacts on affected patients subjected to the long and likely unnecessary courses of multiple antibiotics required for treatment of the disease.

title: liver transplantation: fifty years of experience
display_name: Liver transplantation: Fifty years of experience
abstract: since 1963, when the first human liver transplantation (lt) was performed by thomas starzl, the world has witnessed 50 years of development in surgical techniques, immunosuppression, organ allocation, donor selection, and the indications and contraindications for lt. this has led to the mainstream, well-established procedure that has saved innumerable lives worldwide. today, there are hundreds of liver transplant centres in over 80 countries. this review aims to describe the main aspects of lt regarding the progressive changes that have occurred over the years. we herein review historical aspects since the first experimental studies and the first attempts at human transplantation. we also provide an overview of immunosuppressive agents and their potential side effects, the evolution of the indications and contraindications of lt, the evolution of survival according to different time periods, and the evolution of methods of organ allocation.

title: implementing fast track surgery in hip and knee arthroplasty using the lean six sigma methodology
display_name: Implementing fast track surgery in hip and knee arthroplasty using the lean Six Sigma methodology
abstract: purpose one of the biggest challenges in the health sector is that of costs compared to economic resources and the quality of services. hospitals register a progressive increase in expenditure due to the aging of the population. in fact, hip and knee arthroplasty surgery are mainly due to primary osteoarthritis that affects the elderly population. this study was carried out with the aim of analysing the introduction of the fast track surgery protocol, through the lean six sigma, on patients undergoing knee and hip prosthetic replacement surgery. the goal was to improve the arthroplasty surgery process by reducing the average length of stay (loa) and hospital costs design/methodology/approach lean six sigma was applied to evaluate the arthroplasty surgery process through the dmaic cycle (define, measure, analyse, improve and control) and the lean tools (value stream map), adopted to analyse the new protocol and improve process performance. the dataset consisted of two samples of patients: 54 patients before the introduction of the protocol and 111 patients after the improvement. clinical and demographic variables were collected for each patient (gender, age, allergies, diabetes, cardiovascular diseases and american society of anaesthesiologists (asa) score). findings the results showed a 12.70% statistically significant decrease in los from an overall average of 8.72 to 7.61 days. women patients without allergies, with a low asa score not suffering from diabetes and cardiovascular disease showed a significant a reduction in hospital days with the implementation of the fts protocol. only the age variable was not statistically significant. originality/value the introduction of the fts in the orthopaedic field, analysed through the lss, demonstrated to reduce los and, consequently, costs. for each individual patient, there was an economic saving of 445.85. since our study takes into consideration a dataset of 111 patients post-fts, the overall economic saving brought by this study amounts to 49,489.35.

title: hodgkin lymphoma associated vanishing bile duct syndrome treated successfully with a brentuximab based regimen
display_name: Hodgkin lymphoma associated vanishing bile duct syndrome treated successfully with a brentuximab based regimen

authorships.name: Robert Weishar
institutions: Uniformed Services University of the Health Sciences

abstract: we report a combination therapy to successfully treat a patient with hodgkin s lymphoma complicated by vanishing bile duct syndrome. our patient was in his 20s and presented with jaundice, emesis, b symptoms and diffuse lymphadenopathy along with cholestatic liver injury prompting a liver biopsy, which revealed this diagnosis, after the exclusion of other aetiologies. our treatment regimen incorporated brentuximab along with other more conventional agents which attempted to maximise therapeutic efficacy while minimising the consequences of hepatotoxicity on the treatment protocol. although this patient s treatment course was complicated because of neutropenic infections, the patient achieved a complete metabolic response and is now more than 1 year off therapy.

abstract: biliary atresia (ba), a result from inflammatory destruction of the intrahepatic and extrahepatic bile ducts, is a severe hepatobiliary disorder unique to infancy. early diagnosis and kasai operation greatly improve the outcome of ba patients, which encourages the development of early screening methods. using hplc coupled tandem mass spectrometry, we detected primary bile acids content in dried blood spots obtained from 8 ba infants, 17 neonatal jaundice and 292 comparison infants at 3 4 days of life. taurocholate (tc) was significantly elevated in biliary atresia infants (0.98 0.62 mol/l) compared to neonatal jaundice (0.47 0.30 mol/l) and comparison infants (0.43 0.40 mol/l), with p = 0.0231 and p = 0.0016 respectively. the area under receiver operating characteristic (roc) curve for tc to discriminate ba and comparison infants was 0.82 (95% confidence interval: 0.72 0.92). a cutoff of 0.63 mol/l produced a sensitivity of 79.1% and specificity of 62.5%. the concentrations of total bile acids were also raised significantly in ba compared to comparison infants (6.62 3.89 mol/l vs 3.81 3.06 mol/l, p = 0.0162), with the area under roc curve of 0.75 (95% confidence interval: 0.61 0.89). no significant difference was found between the bile acids of neonatal jaundice and that of comparison infants. the early increase of bile acids indicates the presentation of ba in the immediate newborn period and the possibility of tc as newborn screening marker.

title: learning curve analysis of microvascular hepatic artery anastomosis for pediatric living donor liver transplantation: initial experience at a single institution

abstract: background the incidence of hepatic artery thrombosis in pediatric living donor liver transplantation (ldlt) is significantly higher than that in adults, and is closely related to the surgeon s experience with hepatic artery anastomosis. however, there are few studies on the learning curve of hepatic artery anastomosis among surgeons. methods we collected data related to 75 patients who underwent pediatric ldlt and hepatic artery anastomosis independently by the same surgeon. cumulative sum method (cusum) was used to analyse the duration of hepatic artery anastomosis and determine the cut-off value. patients were divided into two phases according to cusum. we analysed the intraoperative and postoperative data and survival outcomes of the included patients. results total anastomosis duration decreased with an increased number of completed procedures, and the average duration was 42.4 2.20 min. a cut-off value and two phases were identified: 1 43 cases and 44 75 cases. intraoperative blood loss was significantly lower in phase 2 than in phase 1. the immediate functional changes of total bilirubin (tbil) and direct bilirubin (dbil) were significantly also lower in phase 2 than in phase 1. other functional outcomes, postoperative complications, and the long-term survival rate were not significantly different between the two phases. conclusions technical competence in pediatric ldlt hepatic artery anastomosis may be achieved after completing 43 cases. it is a safe procedure with a surgical loupe that can be systematized and adopted by pediatric surgeons with sufficient experience via a relatively long learning curve.

abstract: objective . to date, few studies are available on autoimmune liver disease-associated acute-on-chronic liver failure (aclf). the aim of this study is to investigate bacterial infection and predictors of mortality in these patients. methods . we retrospectively studied patients with autoimmune liver disease from august 2012 to august 2017. clinical data of the patients were retrieved for analysis. results . there were 53 aclf patients and 53 patients without aclf in this study. the aclf group had a higher prevalence of complications ( p 0.05 ). the 28-day and 90-day mortality rates were also obviously high in patients with aclf (38.3% and 74.5%, resp.) ( p 0.05 ). no predictor was significantly associated with 28-day and 90-day transplant-free mortality. in 53aclf patients, 40 (75.5%) patients showed bacterial infection. aclf patients with bacterial infection showed high child-pugh score, meld score, clif-sofa score, 28-day mortality, and 90-day mortality ( p > 0.05 ). moreover, c-reactive protein (crp) using 12.15 mg/l cut-off value proved to be more accurate than procalcitonin in identifying patients with infection. conclusions . autoimmune liver disease-associated aclf showed more complications and high mortality. bacterial infection patients displayed a more severe condition than those without infection. elevated crp is an accurate marker for diagnosing bacterial infection in autoimmune liver disease-associated aclf patients.

title: surgery in pregnancy
display_name: Surgery in Pregnancy
abstract: general guidelines for surgery in pregnancy nonobstetric surgery during pregnancy is of important concern for both the pregnant patient and the fetus. there are limited high-quality data to guide clinical decision-making, given the obvious challenges of performing large-scale randomized clinical trials in this patient population. in general, a pregnant patient should never be denied medically necessary surgery or have life-threatening or urgent surgery delayed, regardless of trimester. delay in clinically indicated (urgent) surgical care can adversely affect both the pregnant patient and the fetus. nonurgent surgery that cannot wait until delivery and is necessary should be performed in the second trimester, if possible. elective surgery, however, should be postponed until after delivery. before nonobstetric surgery is performed, the surgeon should obtain an obstetric consultation because obstetricians are uniquely qualified to discuss aspects of maternal physiology and anatomy that may affect intraoperative maternal-fetal well-being. fortunately, there are no currently used anesthetic agents that have any teratogenic effects in humans when used at standard concentrations at any gestational age. in addition, there is no evidence that in utero exposure to anesthetic or sedative drugs have any effect on the developing fetal brain. the american college of obstetricians and gynecologists recommends consideration for corticosteroid administration in patients with fetuses as viable premature gestational ages due to the potential for preterm labor, in addition to monitoring patients postoperatively for signs of preterm labor. the american college of obstetricians and gynecologists also recommends pregnant patients undergoing nonobstetric surgery be screened for venous thromboembolism risk and have perioperative venous thromboembolism prophylaxis. the decision to use fetal monitoring should be individualized and, if used, should be based on gestational age, type of surgery, and facilities available. if the fetus is considered previable, it is generally not necessary to have fetal monitoring. rather, it is sufficient to ascertain the fetal heart rate by doppler before and after the procedure. however, fetal monitoring may be appropriate when the fetus is viable, and the nature of the planned surgery will allow safe interruption to be able to perform an emergency delivery if needed. if fetal monitoring is recommended, surgery should ideally be performed at an institution with neonatal and pediatric services. in addition, an obstetric care provider with cesarean delivery privileges should be available, and a qualified individual should be readily available to interpret fetal heart rate patterns. appendicitis appendicitis is the most common cause of nongynecological or nonobstetric-related emergency surgery during pregnancy (1). appendicitis occurs in 0.05% 0.07% of pregnancies with the highest frequency of cases occurring during the second trimester. unfortunately, pregnant patients are more likely to experience perforation of the appendix when compared with the general population, with perforation rates as high as 55% vs 4% 19%, respectively (2). during pregnancy, symptoms of appendicitis may appear seemingly normal related to pregnancy, and conventional physical examination techniques such as the rovsing sign (pain in the right lower quadrant with palpation of the left lower quadrant) and psoas sign (pain on passive extension of the right thigh) are largely ineffective because the uterus may push the abdominal wall away from the inflamed appendix (3). rather, nonspecific signs may be more common including abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, and anorexia. in addition, leukocytosis is not reliable given it occurs physiologically during pregnancy (3,4). thus, pregnancy can confound and delay the diagnosis of acute appendicitis. conversely, an incorrect diagnosis of acute appendicitis may result in the removal of a normal appendix (a negative appendectomy), putting the patients at an unnecessary risk of spontaneous abortion and premature delivery (1,5). when a nonpregnant patient displays symptoms indicative of acute appendicitis, a computed tomography (ct) has been demonstrated to be the most accurate method for diagnosis. contrast-enhanced ct have a diagnostic accuracy between 91% and 95% and specificity of 90% 95%. the limitation is that a standard ct scan exposes a pregnant patient and the fetus to radiation. thus, during pregnancy, the american college of radiology recommends initial imaging using ultrasound (us). in nonpregnant patients, us offers 67% 86% sensitivity and 76% 88% specificity (6). however, in pregnant patients, us can visualize the appendix in only 7% of cases with 18% sensitivity and 99% specificity (7). the limitations of us are that it is operator-dependent, and the identification of appendicitis can be obscured by bowel gas and obesity (8). to facilitate ideal us imaging for pregnant patients in their late second or third trimester, patients should be placed in the left posterior oblique or left lateral decubitus positions to allow the use of graded compression techniques while the uterus is displaced (9). if a us diagnosis of acute appendicitis is indeterminate in a pregnant patient, a magnetic resonance imaging (mri) should be used. mri visualizes the appendix with 100% sensitivity and 98% specificity (7). mri does not emit ionizing radiation and has no known adverse effects on either the mother or fetus (10,11). other studies have shown that mri has a positive predictive value of 90.4% and negative predictive value of 99.5%, if the appendix can be identified (6). therefore, mri is the current gold standard for accurately diagnosing appendicitis in pregnant patients after an inconclusive us. (6). when acute appendicitis is diagnosed in a pregnant patient, appendectomy is the treatment of choice. while negative appendectomies can result in a risk of early delivery or fetal loss, delayed appendectomy can result in fetal mortality. a large retrospective review described early delivery in 10% of negative appendectomies and a fetal loss rate of 4% (5). however, a ruptured appendix results in increased fetal mortality. when surgery is performed, both open and laparoscopic appendectomies are considered safe approaches. however, there is some evidence to suggest that laparoscopic interventions should not be performed in the third trimester due to the risks associated with port placement in the setting of a large uterus (12). recent studies have sought to understand the effect of conservative nonoperative management with antibiotics, but the efficacy of surgery is still considered higher and is therefore recommended in this patient population, when indicated (13). biliary tract diseases biliary tract disease is the second most common indication for surgical intervention during pregnancy (14). traditionally, symptomatic biliary tract disease during pregnancy has been managed conservatively. however, high rates of disease recurrence with conservative management have been reported (between 40% and 92%), with 50% developing biliary pancreatitis after conservative management (15,16). advancements in laparoscopic techniques and reports of higher fetal death after conservative management versus laparoscopic cholecystectomy have led to changes in the recommended treatment strategies (17). technical, endoscopic, and surgical advances over the past few decades have shifted management strategy toward a multidisciplinary approach for the management of biliary tract diseases in pregnancy with interventional radiology, interventional gastroenterology for endoscopic retrograde cholangiography (ercp), and laparoscopic surgery, all being used based on the timing of diagnosis and underlying pathology. because there is a risk of pregnancy loss in the first trimester and preterm labor with surgery in the third trimester, laparoscopic cholecystectomy is ideally performed in the second trimester (18 22). in the first and third trimesters, minimally invasive techniques such as percutaneous cholecystostomy and percutaneous gallbladder aspiration can be used. there has been no described morbidity or mortality on using these techniques during pregnancy, and they can be used to bridge the pregnant patient to the second trimester from the first or postpartum from the third trimester (23). pancreatitis regardless of pregnancy status, acute pancreatitis management has largely moved toward a nonoperative approach. acute pancreatitis (ap) during pregnancy is rare but carries high maternal-fetal mortality. up to 60% of ap occurs during the third trimester or the early postpartum period. the most common causes of ap are gallstones (65% 100%), alcohol abuse, post-ercp, and hypertriglyceridemia. although the diagnostic criteria for ap are not specific for pregnant patients, most patients will complain of severe abdominal pain and vomiting and will have significantly elevated serum pancreatic enzymes. the fetal risks from ap during pregnancy are threatened preterm labor, prematurity, and death. a large systematic review reported fetal death in up to 23% of cases and adverse fetal outcomes in up to 57% (24). in cases of ap related to gallstones during pregnancy, a multidisciplinary approach with radiology, obstetrics and gynecology, and general surgery and/or hepatobiliary surgery is advised, and the treatment strategy is based on the trimester. in general, given most pancreatitis cases are mild in the first and second trimesters, treatment with supportive care the in first trimester is warranted with consideration for a laparoscopic cholecystectomy in the second trimester in case of gallstone-induced pancreatitis. however, during the third trimester, conservative treatment or ercp with biliary sphincterotomy (depending on the clinical setting; refer to advanced endoscopy procedures for details [25]), followed by laparoscopic cholecystectomy in the early postpartum period, is recommended (26). trauma trauma occurs in nearly 10% of all pregnancy and is the leading cause of death among pregnant patients. regarding the pregnant patient, surgery for major trauma should proceed as clinically indicated because delaying surgery can often be life-threatening, and without surgical intervention, both the pregnant patient and fetus remain at risk in such cases. the most common traumatic injuries include motor vehicle accidents, assaults, falls, and domestic violence. traumatic injuries are classified as minor or major trauma. fortunately, most traumatic injuries are classified as minor, but even in minor injuries, fetal loss approaches 70%. therefore, after minor trauma, patients should have fetal monitoring for 4 24 hours, and patients should be counseled about the signs and symptoms of placental abruption. when major trauma occurs, patients should ideally be transferred to a trauma center, and monitoring through tocodynamometry should be continued for a minimum of 24 hours if at least 6 uterine contractions have occurred or if the following conditions are found: nonreassuring fetal heart rate patterns, vaginal bleeding, significant uterine tenderness, serious maternal injury, or a positive kleihauer-betke test result (27). regardless of the type of trauma sustained, cardiopulmonary support should be initiated similar to that it is with non-pregnant patients (28). if cardiac arrest occurs and the fundus of the uterus is at the umbilicus or higher a perimortem, cesarean is recommended to improve maternal outcomes with acute care life support (acls) by increasing venous return. the primary reason for this is maternal benefit and it will be performed even if there is intrauterine fetal demise or the fetus is, previable at 20 23 weeks. if the fetus is greater than 23 24 weeks, perimortem cesarean delivery may save the life of the fetus (29,30). in addition, delivery of the fetus increases venous return and cardiac output by 25% 30%, which may lead to a clear survival benefit for the mother (29 31). the american heart association recommends considering perimortem cesarean delivery if acls has not returned spontaneous circulation within 4 5 minutes of cardiac arrest. intestinal obstruction symptoms of intestinal obstruction in pregnancy include abdominal pain (98%), vomiting (82%), and constipation (30%). abdominal tenderness on palpation is found in 71% and abnormal peristalsis in 55% of cases. unfortunately, these are also commonly reported symptoms during pregnancy. thus, abdominal imaging is critical to confirm the diagnosis when bowel obstruction is suspected in pregnant patients. the most common test initially performed is an abdominal x-ray, which can reveal intestinal obstruction in up to 82% of pregnant patients. subsequently, an mri can be useful to determine the etiology of the obstruction (32). intestinal obstruction in pregnant patients is most often due to adhesions (70%), intestinal torsion, colorectal carcinoma, hernia, appendicitis, and other miscellaneous etiologies (33). overall, intestinal obstruction is more often seen in the second and third trimesters, and obstruction related to adhesive disease increases with advanced pregnancy (6% first trimester 28% second trimester; 45% third trimester; and 21% puerperium). treatment will largely depend on the etiology of the obstruction. however, treatment most often begins with conservative management using intravenous fluids and nasogastric tube decompression while performing an evaluation for the etiology of the obstruction. surgical treatment may be necessary in cases where there is hemodynamic compromise, clinical decompensation, complete obstruction on imaging, and worsening pain. if symptoms of fetal anoxia are observed, a cesarean section should be performed before any general surgical intervention. the extent of surgical intervention depends on the intraoperative evaluation. intestinal torsion during pregnancy, more common in later trimesters, mostly occurs in the sigmoid colon and cecum, which may require a partial colonic resection. small bowel torsion secondary to adhesions is diagnosed in 42% of pregnant patients with intestinal obstruction and may simply require lysis of adhesions with or without resection. because the overall prognosis is poor with fetal mortality rates reaching 64%, and those of maternal 6%, surgical intervention should not be delayed because of pregnancy and should proceed as it would in a nonpregnant patient. hepatic lesions liver masses are rarely diagnosed in pregnancy, and the differential diagnosis includes hemangioma, focal nodular hyperplasia (fnh), liver cell adenomas, hepatocellular carcinomas (hccs), and simple cysts and lesions caused by infectious agents (34,35). abdominal us is the imaging modality of choice with a sensitivity of more than 90% for focal liver masses (36). abdominal mri can help differentiate the etiology, even without the use of contrast, and should be considered when us is inconclusive. percutaneous biopsy is debated because of the fear of postprocedure hemorrhage but should be performed if there is a concern for malignancy (35). hemangiomas are the most common hepatic lesions found during pregnancy. they have a strong female predominance and are typically benign. they rarely cause complications when less than 10 cm in size, but there is a small risk (5%) of rupture (34,36). hemangiomas are managed conservatively unless they are >10 cm in size or (34) symptomatic (38 40). when necessary, surgical treatment includes enucleation and resection; however, embolization has also been described (35). fnh is the next most common liver mass discovered in pregnancy. it also has a female predominance, but these lesions do not grow with pregnancy. fnh is also managed expectantly unless it is rapidly enlarging or symptomatic. surgical resection is the treatment of choice when indicated. even if the fnh is monitored, if rapid growth occurs during pregnancy and/or if rapid shrinkage occurs after delivery, the fnh may be estrogen responsive, and consideration should be given to resection before any subsequent pregnancies (35). hepatic adenomas have a 9:1 female: male predominance and are notorious for growing and even rupturing during pregnancy and in the postpartum period. most agree that lesions <5 cm in size can be followed closely, but surgical resection should be considered if there is documented growth due to the concern for rupture. in one report of 26 pregnant patients, 16 of the 26 hepatic adenomas ruptured, and this was associated with a dramatic maternal (7/16) and fetal (6/16) mortality. by contrast, there was no mortality associated with resection of hepatic adenoma during pregnancy. it is important to monitor for growth peripartum as well because rupture is still possible (35,38). the most common malignant liver lesion diagnosed in pregnancy is hcc. hcc is associated with a very poor prognosis, and generally, termination is recommended to allow for aggressive oncologic treatment for the pregnant patient (35,38). the mode of fetal delivery should be based on obstetrical conditions in most patients with liver masses, but cesarean section is generally recommended in patients with hepatic adenomas because of the propensity for rupture at term or immediately postpartum (35). hemorrhoids hemorrhoids are common during pregnancy, as discussed in detail in the articles on constipation, hemorrhoids (41), and fecal incontinence (42) in this monograph. conservative, nonoperative management strategies including dietary changes (water, fiber), stool softeners, ointments, suppositories, toileting and hygiene changes, etc. are the standard of care. operative techniques are reserved only for the most severe complications of hemorrhoids, including acute thrombosis of external hemorrhoids and strangulation of prolapsed internal hemorrhoids. acute hemorrhoid thrombosis can be treated with excision of the hemorrhoidal tissue and removal of clots in the office in the left lateral decubitus position using local injection of anesthetic (43). closed excision of incarcerated internal hemorrhoids has also been described using only local anesthesia and is most often performed in the operating room. in a series of 25 peripartum patients, symptomatic relief was obtained in 24/25 patients with morbidity reported in only 1 patient (significant postoperative hemorrhage). six of the 25 patients required additional interventions after delivery. there are additional interventions such as injection sclerotherapy, rubber band title: o-sialoglycoprotein endopeptidase (osgep) suppresses hepatic ischemia-reperfusion injury-induced ferroptosis through modulating the mek/erk signaling pathway
display_name: O-sialoglycoprotein Endopeptidase (OSGEP) Suppresses Hepatic Ischemia-Reperfusion Injury-Induced Ferroptosis Through Modulating the MEK/ERK Signaling Pathway
abstract: abstract hepatic ischemia reperfusion injury (hiri) was widely accepted as a critical complication of liver resection and transplantation. a growing body of evidence suggested that o-sialoglycoprotein endopeptidase (osgep) was involved in cell proliferation and mitochondrial metabolism. however, whether osgep could mediate the pathogenesis of hiri has still remained unclarified. this study investigated whether osgep could be protective against hiri and elucidated the potential mechanisms. the osgep expression level was detected in cases undergoing ischemia-related hepatectomy and a stable oxygen glucose deprivation/reoxygenation (ogd/r) condition in hepg2 cells. additionally, it was attempted to establish a mouse model of hiri, thus, the function and mechanism of osgep could be analyzed. at one day after hepatectomy, the negative association of osgep expression level with the elevated serum levels of aspartate aminotransferase (ast) and alanine aminotransferase (alt) was noted. moreover, it was attempted to carry out gain- and loss-of-function analyses of osgep in hepg2 cells to reveal its influences on ogd/r-induced injury and relevant signaling pathways. the findings suggested that osgep overexpression significantly protected hepg2 cells against ferroptotic cell death, while osgep consumption had opposite effects. consistent with in vitro studies, osgep deficiency exacerbated liver functions and ferroptotic cell death in a mouse model of hiri. the results also revealed that osgep mediated the progression of hiri by regulating the mek/erk signaling pathway. rescue experiments indicated that erk1/2 knockdown or overexpression reversed the effects of osgep overexpression or knockdown on hepg2 cells under ogd/r condition. taken together, the findings demonstrated that osgep could contribute to alleviate hiri by mediating the mek-erk signaling pathway, which may serve as a potential prognostic marker and a therapeutic target for hiri.

title: xanthogranulomatous inflammation of the peripancreatic region mimicking pancreatic cystic neoplasm
display_name: Xanthogranulomatous Inflammation of the Peripancreatic Region Mimicking Pancreatic Cystic Neoplasm
abstract: xanthogranulomatous inflammation (xgi) is histopathologically characterized by a marked proliferative fibrosis, parenchymal destruction, and infiltration of foamy histiocytes intermixed with other inflammatory cells. herein, we report a case of a 73-year-old man without symptoms who was initially diagnosed with a pancreatic cystic tumor but later with xgi in the peripancreatic region. although xgi has been reported to occur in various organs or tissues, such as the gallbladder, kidney, bone, stomach, colon, appendix, lymph nodes, and soft tissues, xgi involving the pancreas or its surrounding tissues is extremely rare. when a pancreatic cystic lesion does not have typical clinicoradiological features of common pancreatic cystic neoplasms, this pathologic condition should be considered in the differential diagnosis.

title: low-dose biliatresone treatment of pregnant mice causes subclinical biliary disease in their offspring: evidence for a spectrum of neonatal injury
display_name: Low-dose biliatresone treatment of pregnant mice causes subclinical biliary disease in their offspring: Evidence for a spectrum of neonatal injury
abstract: biliary atresia is a neonatal disease characterized by damage, inflammation, and fibrosis of the liver and bile ducts and by abnormal bile metabolism. it likely results from a prenatal environmental exposure that spares the mother and affects the fetus. our aim was to develop a model of fetal injury by exposing pregnant mice to low-dose biliatresone, a plant toxin implicated in biliary atresia in livestock, and then to determine whether there was a hepatobiliary phenotype in their pups. pregnant mice were treated orally with 15 mg/kg/d biliatresone for 2 days. histology of the liver and bile ducts, serum bile acids, and liver immune cells of pups from treated mothers were analyzed at p5 and p21. pups had no evidence of histological liver or bile duct injury or fibrosis at either timepoint. in addition, growth was normal. however, serum levels of glycocholic acid were elevated at p5, suggesting altered bile metabolism, and the serum bile acid profile became increasingly abnormal through p21, with enhanced glycine conjugation of bile acids. there was also immune cell activation observed in the liver at p21. these results suggest that prenatal exposure to low doses of an environmental toxin can cause subclinical disease including liver inflammation and aberrant bile metabolism even in the absence of histological changes. this finding suggests a wide potential spectrum of disease after fetal biliary injury.

title: impact of early reoperation following living-donor liver transplantation on graft survival
display_name: Impact of Early Reoperation following Living-Donor Liver Transplantation on Graft Survival
abstract: observed graft survival for the recipients who underwent reoperation was lower compared to those who did not undergo reoperation, though the result was not significantly different. recipient overall survival with reoperation was comparable to that without reoperation. the present findings enhance the importance of vigilant surveillance for postoperative complication and surgical rescue at an early postoperative stage in the ldlt setting.

title: extreme large for size syndrome after adult liver transplantation: a model for predicting a potentially lethal complication
display_name: Extreme large‐for‐size syndrome after adult liver transplantation: A model for predicting a potentially lethal complication
abstract: there is currently no tool available to predict extreme large for size (lfs) syndrome, a potentially disastrous complication after adult liver transplantation (lt). we aimed to identify the risk factors for extreme lfs and to build a simple predictive model. a cohort of consecutive patients who underwent lt with full grafts in a single institution was studied. the extreme lfs was defined by the impossibility to achieve direct fascial closure, even after delayed management, associated with early allograft dysfunction or nonfunction. computed tomography scan based measurements of the recipient were done at the lower extremity of the xiphoid. after 424 lts for 394 patients, extreme lfs occurred in 10 (2.4%) cases. the 90 day mortality after extreme lfs was 40.0% versus 6.5% in other patients ( p = 0.003). in the extreme lfs group, the male donor female recipient combination was more often observed (80.0% versus 17.4%; p < 0.001). the graft weight (gw)/right anteroposterior (rap) distance ratio was predictive of extreme lfs with the highest area under the curve (area under the curve, 0.95). the optimal cutoff was 100 (sensitivity, 100%; specificity, 88%). the other ratios based on height, weight, body mass index, body surface area, and standard liver volume exhibited lower predictive performance. the final multivariate model included the male donor female recipient combination and the gw/rap. when the gw to rap ratio increases from 80, 100, to 120, the probability of extreme lfs was 2.6%, 9.6%, and 29.1% in the male donor female recipient combination, and <1%, 1.2%, and 4.5% in other combinations. in conclusion, the gw/rap ratio predicts extreme lfs and may be helpful to avoid futile refusal for morphological reasons or to anticipate situation at risk, especially in female recipients. liver transplantation 23 1294 1304 2017 aasld.

title: characteristics of st11 kpc 2 producing carbapenem resistant hypervirulent klebsiella pneumoniae causing nosocomial infection in a chinese hospital
display_name: Characteristics of ST11 KPC‐2‐producing carbapenem‐resistant hypervirulent Klebsiella pneumoniae causing nosocomial infection in a Chinese hospital

authorships.name: Juan Wang
institutions: Hunan Provincial Center for Disease Control and Prevention

authorships.name: Liang Cai
institutions: Hunan Provincial Center for Disease Control and Prevention

abstract: abstract background the purpose of our study is to analyze the microbiological and clinical characteristics of carbapenem resistant hypervirulent klebsiella pneumoniae (cr hvkp) that causes nosocomial infection. methods we collected the carbapenem resistant k . pneumoniae (crkp) strains that caused nosocomial infection in a hospital in china and collected the relevant clinical data. we characterized these strains for their antimicrobial and virulence associated phenotype and genotype and analyzed the clonal relatedness. we screened hypervirulent strains and compared them with non hypervirulent strains. results we retrospectively analyzed 62 crkp strains that caused nosocomial infection in a tertiary hospital within 1 year, of which 41 (41/62, 66.1%) crkp were considered as cr hvkp. all cr hvkp strains were multi drug resistance (mdr) and the vast majority of isolates (39/41, 95.1%) were st11 kpc 2 producing strains. two hypermucoviscous isolates and 4 capsular types were found in 41 cr hvkp. twenty nine isolates (29/41, 70.7%) showed hypervirulence in galleria mellonella infection model. pfge showed that st11 kl47 cr hvkp and st11 kl64 cr hvkp exhibited a high degree of clonality, while non hypervirulent strains were not significant. cr hvkp had higher positive rates of bla kpc 2 and bla ctx m 65 and higher levofloxacin resistance ( p < 0.001, p = 0.005 and p = 0.046, respectively) when compared to the non hypervirulent strains. there was no significant difference between the two groups in terms of in hospital mortality (7/41, 17.1% vs 5/21, 23.8%, p = 0.743). conclusion our research finds that st11 kpc 2 producing cr hvkp is the main type of crkp that caused nosocomial infection, and clonal spread has occurred. we provide more information about cr hvkp in health care.

display_name: A New Approach to Accomplish Intraoperative Cholangiography in Left Lateral Segmentectomy of Living Liver Donation

abstract: background there are 2 main methods of bile duct division in harvesting left lateral segment of a living donor: 1) by intraoperative cholangiography through cystic duct with cholecystectomy, or 2) by direct vision with preoperative magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatography. here, we present a new approach to cholangiography by using the bile duct stump of the fourth liver segment (b4 stump) to achieve left lateral segmentectomy in pediatric living donor liver transplantation. material and methods this was a prospective study of 221 living donors who had undergone intraoperative cholangiography via the b4 stump in the course of left lateral segmentectomy. we collected and analyzed the clinical data, including the success rate of cholangiography by catheterizing the b4 stump; the associated time cost; the classification of the donor liver's biliary anatomy; the number of bile duct orifices on the graft side; and postoperative complications involving the biliary tract. results we were successful in catheterizing b4 stumps in all 221 patients. the mean time cost of these procedures was 7.21 3.62 minutes. variations in the confluence of the right and left lobes were found in 58 patients (26.24%). overall, sludge was detected in 18 cases (8.14%), gallstones were found in 3 patients (1.36%), and a polypoid gallbladder lesion was found in 1 patient (0.45%). there were 11 cases (4.98%) of bile leakage; no biliary strictures were found in the donors. conclusions intraoperative cholangiography via the b4 stump is an alternative procedure for living donors who undergoes left lateral segmentectomy.

title: pediatric hepatocellular carcinoma, a single center study from the south of iran: case series
display_name: Pediatric Hepatocellular Carcinoma, a Single Center Study from the South of Iran: Case Series
abstract: background: hepatocellular carcinoma is a rare tumor in children, thus, there are not many studies regarding clinicopathologic findings of this tumor and no report regarding this tumor in this age group from iran. objectives: in this study, we tried to find out the clinicopathologic findings including outcome of hepatocellular carcinoma in the patients under the age of 18. methods: during the last 10 years (2005 - 2016), we collected all hepatocellular carcinoma cases in the affiliated hospitals of shiraz university of medical sciences (as the largest referral center in the south of iran and the only center of pediatric liver transplantation in the whole country) from the archives of pathology department. next all clinical data were subsequently extracted from the patients' hospital charts. results: we collected 30 cases of hepatocellular carcinoma with the age range of 9 months to 18 years with no significant sex preference. all of the patients, except 3, showed abnormal levels of afp. the most common underlying cause of liver tumorigenesis was type i tyrosinemia. conclusions: hepatocellular carcinoma in children is a rare tumor and is mostly secondary to an underlying liver disease, which is tyrosinemia in our center. hepatitis b related hepatocellular carcinoma is rare in our country, which seems to be related to successful early neonatal vaccination against this viral disease. this tumor has a poor outcome in children and without liver transplantation, has a very short survival rate.

title: elastography improves accuracy of early hepato-biliary complications diagnosis after allogeneic stem cell transplantation
display_name: Elastography improves accuracy of early hepato-biliary complications diagnosis after allogeneic stem cell transplantation
abstract: significant morbidity and mortality have been associated with liver complications after allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (allo-hsct). causes and consequences of these hepato-biliary complications are various and might be life-threatening. a high misdiagnosis rate has been reported because of a weak correlation between clinical, laboratory and imaging data. liver elastography, a liver stiffness measure, is able to assess liver fibrosis and portal hypertension in most liver diseases, but data after allo-hsct are scarce. our aim was to determine the interest of sequential liver stiffness measurements for the diagnosis of early hepatic complications after allo-hsct. over a two years period of time, 161 consecutive adult patients were included and 146 were analyzed. ultrasonography and elastography measurements were performed before transplantation, at day+7 and day+14 by three different experienced radiologists unaware of patients'clinical status. eighty-one (55%) patients had liver involvements within the first 100 days after allo-hsct. baseline elastography was not predictive for the occurrence of overall liver abnormalities. a significant increase in 2d real-time shearwave elastography (2d-swe) was found in patients with sinusoidal obstruction syndrome (sos). fifteen patients (10%) fulfilled ebmt score criteria and twelve (8%) reached baltimore criteria for sos diagnosis, but only six (4%) had a confirmed sos. 2d-swe at day+14 allowed early detection of sos (auroc=0.84, p=0.004) and improved sensibility (75%), specificity (99%) and positive predictive value (60%) over the seattle, baltimore or ebmt scores. a 2d-swe measurement above 8.1kpa at day+14 after allo-hsct seems a promising, non-invasive, and reproducible tool for early and accurate diagnosis of sos.

title: non-alcoholic fatty liver disease in patients with morbid obesity: the gut microbiota axis as a potential pathophysiology mechanism

abstract: abstract background/aim alterations in gut microbiota are associated with the pathogenesis of metabolic diseases, including metabolic-associated fatty liver disease (mafld). the aim of this study was to evaluate gut microbiota composition and functionality in patients with morbid obesity with different degrees of mafld, as assessed by biopsy. subjects/methods 110 patients with morbid obesity were evaluated by biopsy obtained during bariatric surgery for mafld. stool samples were collected prior to surgery for microbiota analysis. results gut microbiota from patients with steatosis and non-alcoholic steatohepatitis (nash) were characterized by an enrichment in enterobacteriaceae (an ethanol-producing bacteria), acidaminococcus and megasphaera and the depletion of eggerthellaceae and ruminococcaceae (scfa-producing bacteria). mafld was also associated with enrichment of pathways related to proteinogenic amino acid degradation, succinate production, menaquinol-7 (k2-vitamin) biosynthesis, and saccharolytic and proteolytic fermentation. basic histological hepatic alterations (steatosis, necroinflammatory activity, or fibrosis) were associated with specific changes in microbiota patterns. overall, the core microbiome related to basic histological alterations in mafld showed an increase in enterobacteriaceae and a decrease in ruminococcaceae . specifically, escherichia coli was associated with steatosis and necroinflammatory activity, whilst escherichia-shigella was associated with fibrosis and necroinflammatory activity. conclusions we established a link between gut microbiota alterations and histological injury in liver diagnosis using biopsy. harmful products such as ethanol or succinate may be involved in the pathogenesis and progression of mafld. thus, these alterations in gut microbiota patterns and their possible metabolic pathways could add information to the classical predictors of mafld severity and suggest novel metabolic targets.
